message.content:
Here are a few popular sushi spots you might want to try in Tokyo:

| Restaurant | Location | Highlights |
|------------|----------|------------|
| **Sukiyabashi Jiro** | Ginza (and other branches) | Legendary chef Jiro Ono; Michelin‑starred, high‑end omakase experience. |
| **Sushi Saito** | Minato | Intimate setting, 3 Michelin stars, renowned for precision and freshness. |
| **Sushi Yoshitake** | Ginza | 3 Michelin stars, meticulous presentation, seasonal ingredients. |
| **Sushi Dai** | Tsukiji Outer Market | Famous for long lines but worth it for fresh tuna and sashimi. |
| **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations | Casual, open‑air counter, great value, open 24/7. |
| **Sushi Kyubey** | Ginza | Classic, high‑quality fish, excellent service. |
| **Sushi Masuda** | Shinjuku | Small, intimate, known for creative rolls and top‑grade fish. |
| **Sushi Iwa** | Roppongi | 2 Michelin stars, modern twists on traditional sushi. |
| **Sushi Takuya** | Shibuya | Known for its “sashimi bar” style, fresh cuts, and friendly staff. |
| **Sushi Kanda** | Minato | 3 Michelin stars, small rooms, focus on seasonal, high‑quality fish. |

If you’re looking for something more casual or budget‑friendly, consider **Sushi Zanmai** or **Sushi Dai** for a quick bite. For a truly unforgettable experience, aim for one of the Michelin‑starred establishments—just remember to book well in advance!
